_comment: Registry of RF_RPCInstance RPC_TYPE ints, used to prevent collisions when scaffolding a new RF_<NAME>_CL/SE mod. RPC_TYPE and MOD_NAME must BOTH be unique per mod (RPC_TYPE is checked first in RF_RPCInstance.OnRPC, MOD_NAME second) — a colliding RPC_TYPE means every colliding mod's Handle() gets exercised on every dispatch before MOD_NAME rejects it, which is wasted work and a correctness risk, not something to imitate.
howToAssignANewId: Read `nextId` below, use it as the new mod's RPC_TYPE, append {"mod": "RF_<NAME>", "rpcType": <nextId>} to `assigned`, then increment `nextId` by 1 and write the file back. Do this as part of scaffolding a new mod (see rf-framework SKILL.md section 13).
historyNote: As of 2026-07-12, every RF_<NAME>_CL/SE mod's RPC_TYPE was renumbered to a unique sequential value starting at RF_AIRDROPS_CL's original value (65874392) and incrementing by 1 in alphabetical order by mod folder name. Previously ~15 mods collided on values copy-pasted from RF_TEMPLATE (e.g. 295226 shared by 12 mods) — see `fixedCollisions` below for the historical record. RF core itself (P:\RF, rpcType 8092347183) was left untouched — it's the framework, not an RF_<NAME> mod, and its value didn't collide with anything.

assigned.note: internals still named RF_TEMPLATE_CL/RF_TEMPLATE_Constant — rename was left incomplete, not fixed here

legacy._comment: Only the RF core framework's own RPC_TYPE remains outside the sequential scheme — it's not an RF_<NAME> mod and wasn't touched by the 2026-07-12 renumbering.

fixedCollisions._comment: Historical record of what was colliding before the 2026-07-12 renumbering. All of these are now resolved — see `assigned` above for current values.
